newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian bonds climb, await Greenspan testimony.
newsitem.headline: Austrian bonds climb, await Greenspan testimony.

text.p: Austrian bonds ended firmer on Tuesday in line with the stronger German Bund future, but traders remained focused on U.S. Fed Alan Greenspan's testimony, due later in the day.
Traders said the cash market lagged by 0.5 to one basis point behind the deutschmark market on meagre volumes.
"You never know what Greenspan will say," said one trader, noting some risk remained for further market development.
Dealers saw upward potential for the German Bund future to 103.15 points after it broke through 103.03.
"But if something comes from Greenspan, then that (projections about the Bund) pure theory," a trader said.
* 10-year benchmark 5.625 pct bond maturing July 2007 up 30 bps at 100.40 to yield 5.57 (5.61) pct in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 100.28/38 to yield 5.59/57 pct.
* Five-year 4.625 bond maturing May 2002 up 25 bps at 100.20 to yield 4.57 (4.63) pct in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 100.04/14 to yield 4.61/59 percent.
* Austrian bond future up 34 bps at 110.24 on turnover of 430 lots.
* 10-year spread over Germany five bps, five-year spread 19 bps.
* Money market rates steady with three-month VIBOR at 3.397 and overnight money weaker at 3.11/3.36. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 257
